response.rationale: The clinical picture of pruritic violaceous annular patches plus biopsy showing lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction indicates a lichenoid interface dermatitis, characteristic of lichen planus. Morphea would typically show thickened collagen rather than a junction-centered lichenoid infiltrate, and granuloma annulare would show necrobiotic granulomas.

rejected.why: Violaceous patch overlap exists, but morphea is not classically severely pruritic and its biopsy shows dermal sclerosis rather than lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction.
Granuloma annulare can be annular, but pruritic violaceous lesions and a lichenoid interface infiltrate are not features; it typically shows necrobiotic palisaded granulomas.
